new_statements.quote: 3. Тональная система не типична для Дагестана. Имеется три тональных уровня: средний (M), высокий (H) и низкий (L). Большинство слов тонировано одним из ровных тонов или некоторой комбинацией ровных тонов. [...] При словоизменении таких корней гласный суффикса либо повторяет тон предшествующего слога, либо имеет свой собственный тон. [...] 4. Словесное ударение отсутствует, фразовое ударение обычно падает на 1-й слог выделяемого слова.
new_statements.translation: 3. The tonal system is untypical for Daghestan. There are three tone levels: mid (M), high (H) and low (L). Most words carry one of the level tones or some combination of level tones. [...] Under inflection of such roots the suffix vowel either repeats the tone of the preceding syllable or has its own tone. [...] 4. Word stress is absent; phrasal stress usually falls on the 1st syllable of the word being emphasised.
new_statements.citation: Kibrik, A. E. & S. V. Kodzasov. 1990. Sopostavitel'noe izuchenie dagestanskix jazykov. Imja. Fonetika. Moskva: Izdatel'stvo Moskovskogo universiteta. Entry '9. Bezhtinskij jazyk (s. Tljadal)', pp. 330-331.
new_statements.locator: p. 331, section 'Slog i prosodija', items 3-4 (entry '9. Bezhtinskij jazyk (s. Tljadal)' begins p. 330)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files opened: (full render of book p.331, running header 'фонетика 331') and, derived from (PDF p.166, 2-up = book pp.330-331). On p.331 under 'СЛОГ И ПРОСОДИЯ' I read item 3 'Тональная система не типична для Дагестана. Имеется три тональных уровня: средний (М), высокий (Н) и низкий (L). Большинство слов тонировано одним из ровных тонов или некоторой комбинацией ровных тонов.... При словоизменении таких корней гласный суффикса либо повторяет тон предшествующего слога, либо имеет свой собственный тон....' and item 4 'Словесное ударение отсутствует, фразовое ударение обычно падает на 1-й слог выделяемого слова.' -- the report's quote is verbatim (its [...] elisions skip the tone examples boq/…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Kodzasov's field description of the Tlyadal variety, Bezhta has no word-level stress; prominence is phrasal and lands on the first syllable of the focused/emphasised word, while syllables carry lexical level tones (H/M/L). Independently, Testelec & Xalilov 1999 (Jazyki mira: Kavkazskie jazyki, p. 305, sec. 2.1.2, same audit folder) state for Bezhta as a whole: 'Prosodicheskie xarakteristiki B. ja. izucheny slabo. Dinamicheskoe udarenie otsutstvuet.' (prosody poorly studied; dynamic stress is absent).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned in either primary source.
new_statements.exceptions: K&K 1990: verbs mostly low level tone, imperatives usually with a falling tone on the last syllable; no stress exceptions since no word stress is posited. Contradicting accounts exist (seen only second-hand via Borise 2018): Madieva 1965:33 weak stress with free variants; Xalilov 1995:394 weak initial stress; Xalilov 2014 initial (phrasal) stress with final stress in vocatives of names, locatives in -ʔ/-t͡ɬ, adverbs in -ʔ and causatives in -(V)ll (Comrie et al. 2015:110), long vowels attracting stress.
new_statements.domain_note: K&K's statement separates word level (no stress; syllabic tone) from phrase level (accent on the initial syllable of the highlighted word); data are isolated citation forms from fieldwork in Tlyadal, with a separate note on the Khoshar-Khota variety (segmental only). Testelec & Xalilov 1999 speak of the language generally (transcription based on Bezhta proper) and only deny 'dynamic' stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990 entry is explicitly the variety of the village Tlyadal (Tljadal), i.e. the Tlyadal dialect of Bezhta (Glottolog lists Bezhta-proper, Khosharkhota and Tlyadal dialects under bezh1248; dialect glottocode not verified here), with a short appended note on Khoshar-Khota. Testelec & Xalilov 1999 describe Bezhta as a whole with Bezhta proper as the transcription base and agree that (dynamic) stress is absent. The competing weak-initial-stress descriptions (Madieva 1965, Xalilov 1995/2014, Comrie et al. 2015) are based on Bezhta proper.

sources.note: Tlyadal Bezhta: three-level tone system (M, H, L) on syllables; 'Slovesnoe udarenie otsutstvuet, frazovoe udarenie obychno padaet na 1-j slog vydeljaemogo slova' = no word stress; phrasal stress usually on the 1st syllable of the focused word (p. 331, Slog i prosodija, items 3-4).

sources.note: Second-hand survey: accounts of Bezhta stress conflict. Madieva 1965:33 weak stress with variants (nísona/nisóna); Kibrik et al. 1978a:44, Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990:331, Testelets & Khalilov 1998:46 say no word stress; Lomtadze 1984 argues for word stress (refuted by Testelets 1993:126 as phrasal intonation); Khalilov 1995:394 initial and acoustically weak; Khalilov 2014:17-19 initial (phrasal) stress on most words (ábo, bówal, bábalo), final in vocatives of names, locatives in -ʔ/-t͡ɬ, adverbs in -ʔ, causatives in -(V)ll (Comrie et al. 2015:110); long vowels seem to attract stress.

sources.citation: Borise, Lena. 2018 draft. Tone and intonation in the languages of the Caucasus. lingbuzz/004204, sec. 2.3.
sources.note: Second-hand: Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990:331 and Kibrik & Testelets 2004:220 analyse Tladal Bezhta as tonal with H, M, L (sora MM 'fox', ãzo HH, biʃe LL, t'iga HM, ħære LM); toneless suffixes copy preceding tone; Kibrik et al. 1978:44 had word-level tone.
